**What was wrong:** Your line (555-123-2002) did not have international roaming turned on. Since you're currently in France, that's why your mobile data was cutting out or crawling along.

**What I did:** I've enabled international roaming on your line at no cost to you. ✅

turns.thought:
No need to worry at all, Mr. Smith — restarting (also called rebooting) your phone will **not** delete anything! 

Here's why, in simple terms:

- Your photos, contacts, messages, and apps are all stored safely in your phone's memory. Turning the phone off and back on doesn't touch them.
- A restart is just like a very short nap for your phone. It closes everything that's running, then opens it all back up again. Everything will be exactly where you left it.
- The only thing you "lose" is a few seconds of time while the phone turns back on. The battery stays, the photos stay — all of it stays.

**How to restart your phone, nice and easy:**
1. Press and **hold the power button** (the button on the side or top) for a few seconds.
2. A menu will appear on the screen — tap **Restart** (or sometimes it says "Reboot").
3. If you don't see "Restart," tap **Power Off**, wait about 10 seconds, then press and hold the power button again to turn it back on.

Alternatively, if you'd rather not do it right now, that's completely fine too. Just wait until you've had a chance to look at your photos one more time and feel ready.

One reassuring note: if the idea still makes you uneasy, you could even restart it while plugged into the charger, so you know the battery won't run down while it's starting back up.

Take your time — there's no rush. Let me know once it's back on and we'll check whether your data is working properly. 😊

turns.thought:
I understand your frustration, Mr. Smith — you've done everything right, and I'm sorry it's still slow. But this is actually a good clue, and I think we can fix it.

That **"2G"** you're seeing is the problem. 2G is a very old, very slow type of connection — like trying to drink a milkshake through a tiny straw. Your phone has accidentally settled onto it. The "Poor" next to it just means the signal it's getting is weak.

**Here's the fix — please do this on your phone:**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**, or **Mobile Network** — it varies by phone).
3. Tap **Mobile Networks**.
4. Look for something called **Network Mode**, **Preferred Network Mode**, or **Network Type**. Tap it.
5. From the list, choose **5G/4G/3G auto** or **4G/5G preferred** — anything that mentions **4G or 5G**. Make sure it is *not* set to "2G" or "3G only."

Your phone will then go looking for a faster network and should switch over within a few seconds.

**If your phone doesn't have that setting, or if it still says 2G after changing it:**
- Take a few steps, ideally nearer a window or outside. Being indoors, or in a basement or old stone building (very common in France!), can weaken the signal a lot.
- Then turn your phone off and on again, just like you did before — that worked well for you last time.

One thing I'd gently set your expectations about: even on 4G or 5G, mobile data while abroad can feel a bit slower than what you're used to at home, so it may not be lightning fast. But it should be *much* better than 2G — enough for email, maps, and looking at photos.

Please try those steps and tell me what the top of your screen says afterward. You're doing great — we'll get there. 😊

- If you see a VPN that is connected, tap it and choose **Disconnect** or turn it **OFF**

turns.thought:
Yes, Mr. Smith — you've found it! That VPN is almost certainly what's slowing you down. The "poor" performance note it's showing is a strong sign. Let's turn it off.

**First, let me put your mind at rest about what a VPN is:**

A VPN is a privacy tool. When it's on, your internet traffic takes a long detour through another computer somewhere else in the world before reaching its destination. Think of it like posting a letter to a friend by first sending it to another country, having someone there forward it on. It still arrives — but it takes much longer.

**Turning it off will not break anything.** Here's the reassuring part:
- It won't delete your photos or anything else — ⚠️ nothing gets removed
- All your apps, messages and contacts stay exactly as they are
- The only change is your internet goes back to the direct, faster route
- You can always switch it back on later if you ever want to

You're not damaging anything at all.

**Here's how to turn it off, gently:**

*If you have an Android phone (Samsung, Google Pixel, etc.):*
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Connections**
3. Tap **More connection settings**
4. Tap **VPN**
5. You should see your VPN listed — tap the little **gear/cog icon** beside it
6. Tap **Disconnect**
7. If instead you see a **switch** (on/off), just tap it so it goes **grey/OFF**

*If you have an iPhone:*
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **General**
3. Tap **VPN & Device Management**
4. Tap **VPN**
5. Tap the **Status** switch so it goes **grey/OFF**, or tap **Disconnect**

Once it's off, please run your speed test again and tell me the number. I have a good feeling about this one. 😊

And take your time — I'm here, and there's no rush at all.
